baseline: Cooldown Counter design baseline v0.1 with implementation decisions in docs/data-model.md
executionPolicy: Only actual clean passed results in every required browser project count as proven. Missing, skipped, flaky and failed executions do not count.

stories.title: Sign in to restricted records
stories.acceptance: The actual login form restricts access, reports generic rejected credentials and distinguishes network unavailability.

stories.title: Correct missing login inputs
stories.acceptance: Both missing, username missing and password missing produce distinct messages that clear during correction.

stories.title: Resume a valid session
stories.acceptance: The server cookie restores identity after reload and shared-cookie tabs reconcile another login.

stories.title: End the operator session
stories.acceptance: Logout invalidates protected access and removes old records and unfinished dialogs from mounted tabs.

stories.title: Limit records to permitted operators
stories.acceptance: Anonymous access, missing CSRF, foreign fleet IDs and viewer writes are rejected by the actual API.

stories.title: Navigate the fleet workspace
stories.acceptance: Calendar, Accounts, Cooldowns and newly created account detail are reachable with matching visible headings.

stories.title: Assess fleet totals
stories.acceptance: The displayed recorded and active totals match one unique event and one restricted account despite repeated calendar segments.

stories.title: Find a tracked account
stories.acceptance: A UUID-selected hbh_1 does not include hbh_10, and trimmed case-insensitive account search finds the expected account.

stories.title: Focus by cooldown status
stories.acceptance: Active and clear account filters show the matching distinct accounts under combined offence selection.

stories.title: Focus by offence type
stories.acceptance: Two offence checkboxes retain their selections and use union semantics with status filtering.

stories.title: Restore an unfiltered workspace
stories.acceptance: Reset clears exact account, text, status and offence restrictions so excluded accounts return.

stories.title: Review cooldowns by day
stories.acceptance: A real seven-day event renders across week boundaries without multiplying its saved identity.

stories.title: Review future step-down dates
stories.acceptance: Forecast entries have distinct accessible names and the API returns the terminal ladder's future reduction facts.

stories.title: Reach crowded calendar records
stories.acceptance: A week with six overlapping events exposes hidden entries through an operable disclosure.

stories.title: Browse calendar history and later months
stories.acceptance: Explicit month navigation and earliest-history navigation reach records outside the initial range without requiring scrolling.

stories.title: Return to the present
stories.acceptance: Jump reveals the owning NOW anchor and reset restores the default calendar range.

stories.title: Focus an account from the calendar
stories.acceptance: Activating a recorded bar chooses its exact account UUID in the account filter.

stories.title: Compare account availability
stories.acceptance: The account list distinguishes active, expired and no-history accounts with readable states.

stories.title: Reach later accounts
stories.acceptance: An explicit load action reveals accounts beyond the first twelve rows.

stories.title: Inspect one account
stories.acceptance: Detail shows the selected account's exact tag, SteamID and preserved history.

stories.title: Open the external Steam account
stories.acceptance: The Steam link contains the exact full digit sequence; tests do not open the external site.

stories.title: Compare per-offence predictions
stories.acceptance: Every configured offence has its own named prediction and initial step.

stories.title: Understand a prediction
stories.acceptance: No-history and saved-state/clean-state explanations appear beside the corresponding account estimates.

stories.title: Audit recorded observations
stories.acceptance: History separates observed remaining minutes, assigned total and transition/override explanation.

stories.title: Start an observation report
stories.acceptance: The shared report action opens a named dialog with the selected real account and offence.

stories.title: Leave an unfinished report
stories.acceptance: Preview followed by Cancel closes the report without appending any event.

stories.title: Identify the report account
stories.acceptance: Report account search identifies the intended exact SteamID and selection.

stories.title: Identify the observed offence
stories.acceptance: Report offence search finds the expected category by its code and selects the correct UUID.

stories.title: Locate an observation in time
stories.acceptance: Issue and observation instants are distinct UTC facts, and future input does not become a report.

stories.title: Enter observed time remaining
stories.acceptance: Positive remaining evidence stays separate from total; 1 day plus 2 hours plus 3 minutes saves as 1563 minutes.

stories.title: Correct invalid remaining input
stories.acceptance: Zero, negative and fractional remaining input shows correction feedback without fabricated saved evidence.

stories.title: Understand the predicted report total
stories.acceptance: The genuine server preview returns the step and total that an unchanged accepted save preserves.

stories.title: Record a known ladder step
stories.acceptance: A real ladder step can be chosen with an attributed reason and reset to prediction.

stories.title: Resolve evidence that exceeds the estimate
stories.acceptance: Over-total evidence warns, offers the first fitting step when present and cannot be saved above every step.

stories.title: Record a validated observation
stories.acceptance: An accepted report redirects to its account, persists evidence and acknowledges an identical retry without another event.

stories.title: Prevent invalid observation references
stories.acceptance: No active types disables reporting, and even an owner cannot substitute another fleet's account UUID.

stories.title: Inspect offence ladders
stories.acceptance: All configured ladders and the transition-rule reference are available for inspection.

stories.title: Start with the designed offence catalogue
stories.acceptance: The five editable seed ladders match the recorded design baseline and do not fabricate account history.

stories.title: Predict escalation independently per account and offence
stories.acceptance: Accounts and offence types have independent histories, with one advance and a final-step cap.

stories.title: Account for clean-time decay
stories.acceptance: Seven elapsed days from expiry decays at the exact boundary, but one millisecond before does not.

stories.title: Evaluate observations in historical order
stories.acceptance: A backdated report is assessed at its issue time while existing accepted assessments remain immutable.
stories.decisionNotes: Chronological event-time assessment is retained; accepted earlier snapshots are not replayed into different historical results.

stories.title: Add an offence type
stories.acceptance: A new named offence and nonempty duration ladder are created through the actual editor and API.

stories.title: Prevent ambiguous offence type names
stories.acceptance: Empty and case-insensitive duplicate names are rejected without publishing partial records.

stories.title: Update offence labels and trigger notes
stories.acceptance: Saved metadata is trimmed/normalized and literal note markup remains text.

stories.title: Rename an offence type without losing history
stories.acceptance: A renamed offence keeps its UUID and history while current labels follow the new name.

stories.title: Edit a ladder step duration
stories.acceptance: Minute/hour editing stores explicit whole-minute steps and rejects a zero duration.

stories.title: Change the number of escalation steps
stories.acceptance: Step addition/removal renumbers draft positions, protects the final step and discards a cancelled draft.

stories.title: Review offence type deletion impact
stories.acceptance: Fresh archival confirmation replaces destructive deletion and preserves every event and observation.
stories.decisionNotes: Archival replaces the prototype cascade delete. Destructive deletion and its atomic requirements are intentionally not claimed.

stories.title: Use an alternative decay policy if approved
stories.acceptance: Full reset and no-decay are explicit policy choices; start anchoring and uncalibrated confidence remain excluded.
stories.decisionNotes: Only expiry anchoring is supported. Full-reset/no-decay are explicit controls; code-only start anchoring and confidence labels are not implemented.

stories.title: Understand the impact of a model change
stories.acceptance: Policy publication and backdated evidence preserve old assessment snapshots instead of silently recalculating history.
stories.decisionNotes: Immutable policy/assessment history replaces a retrospective recalculation impact workflow. Original recalculation criteria are not claimed.

stories.title: Retain recorded history
stories.acceptance: Accepted history survives page reload and a complete logout/login cycle.

stories.title: Review the group's accepted history
stories.acceptance: An authorized viewer reads shared evidence and an editor contributes with their own attribution while role limits remain enforced.

stories.title: Recover an interrupted change
stories.acceptance: Failed report and configuration writes retain drafts; deliberate retries and stable event identities avoid duplicate offences.

stories.title: Resolve changes during reporting
stories.acceptance: A genuine intervening write causes a stale-preview conflict and requires re-review before accepting a changed revision.

stories.title: Recover when access expires
stories.acceptance: Expired cookies recover on the first deliberate login, and session changes remove the prior user's unfinished report.

stories.title: Distinguish observation from derived estimate
stories.acceptance: Observed evidence, model totals, overrides and mutation authors remain distinguishable without exposing credentials.

stories.title: Use the tracking workflow without a mouse
stories.acceptance: Keyboard account activation, range selection and submit complete a genuine protected report.

stories.title: Choose an override on a touch device
stories.acceptance: A touch-enabled browser selects an existing override step using the production range control.

stories.title: Navigate modal reporting with assistive technology
stories.acceptance: The modal is named, keeps keyboard focus inside while open and restores its launcher after Escape.

stories.title: Understand report controls without visual guessing
stories.acceptance: Native labels identify report fields and controls for keyboard-driven operation.

stories.title: Perceive status and validation feedback
stories.acceptance: Textual states and announced validation remain understandable after severity colors are removed.

stories.title: Reach tracking information on supported screens
stories.acceptance: The user-confirmed desktop/mobile contract is exercised at 320, 390, 768, 1024 and 1440 CSS pixels with 100-percent and 200-percent text: calendar, account list/detail, report and type-editor information/actions stay reachable.

stories.title: Use equivalent interactions with reduced motion
stories.acceptance: The reduced-motion browser preference retains equivalent modal and present-day navigation outcomes.

stories.title: Understand delayed or failed data loading
stories.acceptance: Unavailable data and login service states differ from empty/rejected results and recover through real retries.

stories.title: Keep an offence distinct from its observations
stories.acceptance: A second observation attaches to the existing cooldown without another offence or ladder advancement.

atomicRequirements.rule: This manifest maps outcome acceptance. It does not claim all 363 atomic criteria. All RQ IDs without a reviewed assertion mapping are listed as not independently mapped in the generated evidence.

dispositionMeanings.browser_assertion: An exact E2E assertion is mapped. Passed proof still requires actual clean results on all required projects.
dispositionMeanings.test_assertion: An exact backend/unit/component assertion is mapped. This report does not evaluate its execution.
dispositionMeanings.implementation_inspected: Relevant source was inspected. The narrow acceptance condition is not independently proven by the current mapping.
dispositionMeanings.user_alternative: A user-selected policy replaces conflicting prototype behavior. Only the replacement may be tested and claimed.
dispositionMeanings.implementation_assumption: An explicit implementation substitution, with related equivalent behavior evidence, needs product review. It is not user approval.
dispositionMeanings.implementation_gap: A concrete missing source behavior is being fixed; it is not deferred or claimed as implemented.
dispositionMeanings.decision_pending: The candidate depends on an unapproved supported-environment or accessibility contract; smoke checks do not establish broad conformance.

limits: Static manifest validation proves references, not behavior. Execution proof requires actual Playwright JSON and, for lower-layer assertions, matching pytest JUnit or Vitest JSON reports.
API fixture provisioning uses real authenticated endpoints and one unique fleet per case. No mocked API responses are used in full-stack tests.
Offline browser tests simulate real connection failures; they do not prove production disaster recovery or lost-response behavior for every mutation.
Functional keyboard, touch, noncolor, reduced-motion and narrow-layout checks do not certify WCAG, contrast or assistive-technology conformance.
Rule defaults are editable model inputs, not verified current Valve or CS2 policies.
Official integrations, deployment capacity and backup restoration require separate evidence and are not claimed by these outcomes.

supportedEnvironment.limits: Representative responsive interaction checks do not claim every possible width, assistive technology or WCAG certification.
